topic: Gravity and its effects on motion
key_concepts: Gravity is a force of attraction between any two objects.
Gravitational force pulls objects toward each other and toward Earth's center.
Isaac Newton proposed the theory of gravity in 1687 after observing a falling apple.
Earth's gravity pulls dropped or thrown objects back to the ground.
Gravity keeps objects on Earth's surface from floating away.
Gravity keeps planets orbiting the Sun and moons revolving around planets.
Without gravity, objects on Earth would float and heavenly bodies could collide.
Gravity affects all objects in the universe, not only solid objects.
Jumping or lifting an object requires overcoming gravity.
Moving against gravity includes actions like an airplane taking off or lifting a box.
